svg.text: F Sub-mechanisms (4) — rolling, fixing, eggs, and handling at the hob
Each panel loops on its own.
source: F-first-principles.md section 6
S17/S18 cold plate: see F-zustand
S14 Loop roller for Rouladen

g.text: pull one side of a slack loop:
the content rolls up on itself

svg.text: Cigarette and vine-leaf roller principle: Rouladen, cabbage rolls,
mince logs, dough logs, Swiss rolls.
Feasibility H for rolling, M for where the seam ends up
S15 Magnetic pins

g.text: press axis drives Ø2 × 90 pins from a magazine
at plating a magnet pulls each pin by its ring

svg.text: Ferritic stainless pins; the machine counts pins out against pins in,
so none stays in the food.
Feasibility H
S16 Ice-weld seam

g.text: closed roll, seam down, 3–4 min: the seam freezes shut
seam-down into the hot pan: it sears before it thaws

svg.text: Wet meat surfaces frozen together stick; coagulated protein then
takes over. No tie, no pin, nothing to remove.
Feasibility M–L: does the seam survive a 2-hour braise?
S22 Egg by vacuum

g.text: bellows cups hold the ends (40 kPa → 20 N)
blade scores the equator from below (0.1 J)
cups part 15 mm and tilt: content drops
clear cup on a scale: checked, then committed

svg.text: Shells never leave the cups until over the waste chute; one bad egg
costs one egg, not the dough. Yolk separated by a soft Ø25 tip.
Feasibility M–H
S20 Double-pan flip

g.text: preheated, oiled empty pan placed face down
pair clamped, turned 180° about one axis
upper pan lifted: everything turned at once

svg.text: Pancake, omelette, Rösti, fish, six Frikadellen, a Schnitzel:
nothing has to get under the food. Flipping blocks 12.9 % of meals.
Feasibility H; hot fat < 30 mL or drained first
S41 Venturi drain wand
Drain by removing the water, not the food: no moving part, the
motive water flushes the ejector; 4 L pasta pot in ~70 s.
Feasibility H
